inventory.description: One full-length, cartoon-styled human figure on the left faces right toward the other figure. The mouth is open. The figure has a head with hair, facial features and an ear, a horizontally striped collared shirt, two lowered arms and hands, trousers, and two shoes. Feet are separated; no held object or contact with the other figure is shown.

One full-length, cartoon-styled human figure on the right faces left toward the first figure. Hair, facial features and ear are visible. The shirt has a checked pattern and collar; both arms and hands are lowered, with trousers and two shoes below. No instrument, cable, tube or shared object links the figures.

Between the faces are six separate source ink strokes: two small separated marks nearest the left person's mouth, followed by four taller, approximately upright curved strokes toward the right person. These are schematic sound-propagation marks, not six measured wave cycles. Their irregular spacing and shape supply no wavelength, frequency, time or calibrated distance.

relationships: The two figures face one another and remain physically separated.
The left open mouth, intervening schematic marks and right-facing-inward listener form the qualitative communication arrangement.
No physical arrow direction, sound speed or numerical scale is encoded in the PNG.

routingPlan.reason: Human appearance and communication roles are semantic artwork; preserve the source's separate schematic propagation marks in a deterministic overlay rather than asking generation to invent arrows, wavelengths or wave counts.
routingPlan.artworkScope: Two contemporary, culturally neutral people facing each other, left speaking and right listening. Preserve full figures and separation, not obsolete caricature or old-book texture. Artwork excludes propagation marks, labels and arrows.
routingPlan.deterministicScope: The source schematic propagation marks between the speaking mouth and listening-side head, with their source identity and non-measured status retained.
futureAssertions: Two semantic human objects, with separate non-overlapping occupied regions.
Propagation overlay occupies the gap between the figures without covering either face.
No arrowheads, scale, measured intervals or new labels.
Source stroke identities remain individually mapped; no claim of measured wave count.
routingPlan.notDecorative: This is a sound-transmission teaching illustration, not a portrait.
routingPlan.generationPremise: Any future artwork call requires the full frozen modern text, independent SCI readiness and the existing authorized n-azure method/cost boundary. No call or spend occurred during this inventory.

uncertainties: The two short marks nearest the mouth are separate printed strokes; their interpretation as parts of a complete front or a particular waveform is not determined by the source.

inventory.description: A short, thick horizontal support bar is near the upper-left corner. A small dark attachment or knot below it joins a long thin vertical suspension line.

One approximately vertical thin dark thread runs down from the upper attachment to the lower suspended object. It remains continuous through the level from which the enlargement leader leaves. There is no tension label or force arrow along it.

One elongated, roughly rectangular hanging weight is attached at the bottom by a dark knot or connector. The object has a dark outline/body and a narrow lighter vertical interior portion. The pixels do not establish its material, mass or exact three-dimensional cross-section.

One oblique solid leader starts on the lower-middle part of the thread and ends with an arrowhead at the left side of the circular enlargement. It identifies the magnified region; it is not a force, displacement, flow or propagation-speed arrow.

One outlined circular magnification frame lies to the right of the thread, above the hanging weight. The leader points to its left boundary. No numerical magnification or dimensional equivalence between this frame and the apparatus is given.

The circular frame contains repeated near-round black atomic glyphs in horizontally staggered rows, with white interstices. Top and bottom rows include cut-off glyph portions; several peripheral glyphs join the circular outline. The source contains approximately round silhouettes rather than marked mathematical centers, calibrated distances, bonds or an identified crystal lattice.

relationships: Support, upper attachment, continuous thread, lower attachment and weight form one connected suspension apparatus.
The single oblique enlargement leader connects the thread region to the circular frame, not to one chosen atom.
Atomic glyphs are contained within or clipped by the circular frame and have visible gaps between them.
No source force-vector network, motion state, time sequence, wavelength or physical scale is present.
The original historical explanation is source text, not a new claim that atoms are separated by literally empty regions or that the picture proves instantaneous action.

routingPlan.reason: The source is an apparatus-and-magnification schematic. Support, thread, weight, leader, circular frame, atomic glyphs and gaps are geometric teaching objects; natural material appearance is not the instructional content.
futureAssertions: Exactly one enlargement leader has the source thread-to-frame endpoint relationship.
The leader is not relabeled or duplicated as a force arrow.
The atom group stays inside or deliberately source-clipped at the circular frame.
Source glyph identities and staggered-row relationships must be mapped before finalizing deterministic objects; do not replace them with a newly chosen regular lattice.
routingPlan.regularizationLimit: Clean linework is permitted later; measured geometry, bond edges, coordinate axes and a newly specified lattice are not source facts.

uncertainties: An exact total and per-row listing of full versus clipped atomic glyphs is not reliably resolved where perimeter ink merges with glyphs. This is an explicit unresolved source-geometry item, not permission to invent missing atoms.
The weight silhouette does not uniquely distinguish a rectangular block from a cylindrical or other three-dimensional hanging mass.
